data.description:
## Context / Problem
`src/rebar/llm/code_review/bugfix_size_gate.py:42` escalates a bug fix to plan review only above 150 non-test lines. A backtest over 641 bug-fix commits on `origin/main` since 2026-06-15 (29 later introduced a bug; corpus from `scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py --rev-range origin/main`) shows the floor catches 9 of 29. No signal computable from the diff beats it (file count, package spread, touched-function cyclomatic complexity, module fan-in, new-file: 3–12 of 29). The signal that does work is repeat fixing: a fix to a file that was bug-fixed at least twice in the prior 7 days catches 17 of 29 at 37% escalation; these are families fixed one instance at a time (`8d862d1058`, a 127-line fix, introduced five bugs). The rule is pure git history plus ticket type — no path lists — so it holds on any project and scales with that project's churn. Approved 2026-08-21.

## Approach
Add a second escalation predicate beside the line floor in `bugfix_size_gate.py`: for each non-test file in the diff, count commits on the base branch in the prior 7 days that (a) touch the file and (b) carry a `rebar-ticket:` trailer or leading id resolving to a `bug` ticket (reuse `extract_ticket_refs` and the resolver the backtest already uses); escalate when any file's count is ≥ 2. Parameters `REPEAT_FIX_WINDOW_DAYS = 7` and `REPEAT_FIX_MIN_PRIOR = 2` sit beside `BUGFIX_SIZE_THRESHOLD_NON_TEST_LINES`. Mirror the predicate in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py:191-211` (`bug_blast_radius_escalates`) so `review-plan` on a bug runs the full rubric under the same condition. The teaching finding names the file and the prior fixes. Extend `scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py` to emit the repeat-fix flag so the rule stays backtestable with the gate's own code.

## Scope
`src/rebar/llm/code_review/bugfix_size_gate.py`, `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py`, `scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py`, `docs/plan-review-gate.md` (escalation section), `tests/unit/llm/code_review/test_bugfix_size_gate.py`, `tests/unit/plan_review/test_bug_escalation.py`.

## Testing
Happy path: a fixture repo where a file has two prior bug-trailer commits inside 7 days escalates a 20-line fix; a file with one prior fix, or two fixes 8+ days old, does not. Edge: prior commits without a resolvable bug trailer do not count; merge commits do not count; the line floor still escalates independently. Pinning: existing `bugfix_size` tests and `--check-planning-corpus` pass unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A bug fix touching a file with ≥2 bug-trailer commits in the prior 7 days is escalated on both the code-review gate and `review-plan`; checked by the new unit tests.
- [ ] `python scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py --rev-range origin/main` reports the repeat-fix flag per commit and, over the 641-commit corpus, flags 17 of the 29 labelled commits; checked by running it and comparing to the corpus in this review's scratch data attached to the ticket.
- [ ] The planning-corpus check still passes (`--check-planning-corpus` exit 0); checked by running it.
data.title: Escalate repeat fixes to plan review: a file bug-fixed twice in the prior 7 days
